headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading errors: ComfyUI can write model/workflow files while transformers can read/write files and run code, creating unsafe shared-pipeline interactions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and has no clipboard/MCP/browser surfaces, so direct injection paths are limited. transformers can read stdin/stdout and files, so if ComfyUI outputs are manually copied or piped into it, prompt-like content could influence downstream processing. This is a weak, mostly manual bridge rather than a default shared channel.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies ComfyUI-generated text into transformers prompts or scripts, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared file or pipe is introduced between the agents, content from ComfyUI can be interpreted by transformers.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting generated text into downstream prompts.
Use a strict file format with schema validation.
Add a human review step before any downstream parsing.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, workflows, seeds, and model artifacts, while transformers reads files and has broad network egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive media or workflow data can flow from ComfyUI into transformers and then out to external services. The pair does not show explicit isolation, so leakage is plausible in default multi-tool setups.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, transformers can read ComfyUI artifacts.
IF transformers sends loaded file contents to remote inference or hub services, those artifacts may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Disable network access for transformers when handling sensitive files.
Store ComfyUI outputs in a non-shared export folder.
Review file lists before running transformers.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem sandboxing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI writes model/workflow files and supports multiple instances only via an asynchronous queue, while transformers can execute shell commands, install packages, read/write files, and spawn subprocesses. If both target the same directory, concurrent writes and state corruption are realistic, and transformers can overwrite artifacts ComfyUI depends on. The overlap is broad and dangerous by default in shared workspaces.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same model or workflow directory, file races can occur.
IF transformers modifies files ComfyUI expects to remain stable, pipeline state can be corrupted.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories.
Run only one writer at a time.
Make shared assets read-only.
Snapshot the workspace before batch runs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared model paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI produces workflows, seeds, and model artifacts that transformers can consume as inputs or scripts. transformers can then act on those inputs with shell and subprocess authority, so an error or hallucinated artifact from ComfyUI can propagate into downstream processing without verification. The pair lacks an explicit validation boundary, making cascading mistakes plausible.
conditions: IF transformers consumes ComfyUI outputs without validation, incorrect workflows can propagate.
IF downstream scripts trust generated filenames or parameters, erroneous actions can be triggered.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents.
Whitelist acceptable file names and parameters.
Require human approval for generated workflows.
Log and diff all intermediate artifacts.
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between producer and consumer.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and show no explicit regulated-data certifications or residency constraints, so there is no documented compliance mismatch. However, ComfyUI handles media artifacts and transformers can transmit file contents over broad network egress, so a compliance issue could arise if regulated data is introduced into the pair. The other agent is cited because the risk depends on their interaction.
conditions: IF regulated media or personal data is processed through the shared pipeline, retention and residency controls must be checked.
IF transformers uploads those artifacts to external services, policy obligations may be triggered.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Disable outbound network for regulated workloads.
Document retention and deletion handling.
Review vendor terms before deployment.
requires-engineering: implement data-class routing controls.
